subject: general
question: The price of fuel decreases by 30%, 40% and 45% in three successive months, but increases by 65% in the fourth month. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the price of fuel in the fourth month as compared to its original price? (Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Take initial price = 100

After 30% decrease ⇒ 70

After 40% decrease ⇒ 70 × 0.60 = 42

After 45% decrease ⇒ 42 × 0.55 = 23.1

After 65% increase ⇒ 23.1 × 1.65 = 38.115

**∴ Net change = 38.115 − 100 = −61.89%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Successive changes: −30%, −40%, −45%, +65%

**Formula used:**

New value = Original × successive multipliers

**Calculation:**

⇒ Assume initial price = 100

⇒ After 30% decrease: 100 × 0.70 = 70

⇒ After 40% decrease: 70 × 0.60 = 42

⇒ After 45% decrease: 42 × 0.55 = 23.1

⇒ After 65% increase: 23.1 × 1.65 = 38.115

⇒ Net change = 38.115 − 100 = −61.885

⇒ Percentage change ≈ −61.89%

**∴ The price decreases by 61.89%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

Use multipliers: (1 ± rate/100)

Net Effect

Compare final value with original

Shortcut

Assume base value = 100 for easy calculation
